articles.headline: Sport on ESPN in Africa this festive - What to watch on DStv, Disney+ in December
articles.description: From Thanksgiving NFL showdowns, to Christmas Day NBA action, and Boxing Day football, ESPN Africa has the festive season covered with a packed line-up of live sport, on channels across the continent and Disney+ in SA.
articles.body:
From the excitement of Thanksgiving NFL games to Christmas Day basketball, college football bowl games, and international football fixtures, ESPN and ESPN2 will bring audiences some of the biggest names and rivalries in sport throughout November and December.

With the National Football League (NFL) season gathering momentum and the road to Super Bowl LXI heating up, American football will be a major highlight of the holiday programming, alongside a host of other exciting sporting fixtures.

Thanksgiving kicks off the action

Thanksgiving on Nov. 26 will deliver a triple helping of NFL action, starting with the Detroit Lions taking on the Chicago Bears at 20:00, followed by the Dallas Cowboys against the Philadelphia Eagles at 23:30. The Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs will round off the Thanksgiving line-up in the early hours of Friday, 27 November at 03:15. All three games will air live on ESPN.

Black Friday will keep the sporting excitement going with Turkish Süper Lig football as Alanyaspor face Konyaspor at 18:56, followed by English Football League action between Southampton and Middlesbrough at 21:52, both on ESPN.

Christmas brings the best of American sport

Christmas week will see the action continue with college football's New Mexico Bowl on Christmas Eve at 21:30 on ESPN2, followed by the Hawai'i Bowl at 02:00 on Christmas Day. NFL fans can look forward to the Philadelphia Eagles facing the Houston Texans at 03:15 on Christmas Day on ESPN, while the Seattle Seahawks will take on the Los Angeles Rams at 03:15 on 26 December on ESPN2, as the battle for playoff places intensifies.

Basketball fans will also be treated to a Christmas Day NBA triple-header, beginning with the New York Knicks against the San Antonio Spurs at 19:00, followed by the Boston Celtics versus the Miami Heat at 21:30 and the Los Angeles Lakers taking on the Philadelphia 76ers at 00:00 on 26 December, all live on ESPN.

For a different take on the opening game, ESPN2 will also broadcast NBA Dunk the Halls, a special Disney-themed alternate presentation of the Knicks versus Spurs match at 19:00.

Boxing Day delivers even more action

The festive sporting action will continue on Boxing Day, Saturday, 26 December, with English Football League action as Blackburn Rovers face Birmingham City at 16:52, followed by Scottish Premiership football between Kilmarnock and Rangers at 19:40, both on ESPN. College football fans can enjoy the Pinstripe Bowl at 19:00 and Duke's Mayo Bowl at 22:30 on ESPN2, while another NFL Week 16 fixture will air on ESPN at 23:30.

The holiday sporting action will be broadcast on ESPN (Azam 120, DStv 218, StarTimes 248, Wananchi / Zuku TV 712, ZAP 31) and ESPN2 (Azam 121, DStv 219, StarTimes 249, Wananchi / Zuku TV 713, ZAP 32), as well as on the ESPN and ESPN2 linear channels on Disney+ in South Africa.

How to watch ESPN

ESPN: Azam 120, DStv 218, StarTimes 248, Wananchi / Zuku TV 712, ZAP 31

ESPN2: Azam 121, DStv 219, StarTimes 249, Wana

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: AC Milan to land Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk?
articles.description: AC Milan are monitoring the situation of Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk could move to AC Milan on a free transfer in the summer, while Manchester United are interested signing in Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AC Milan are monitoring the situation of Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk, with plans to reinforce their defense in the next two transfer windows, according to Tuttosport. The 35-year-old is reported to be eyeing a spell in Italy, and enters the final six months of his contract in January, but Corriere dello Sport reports that Milan are also tracking Sporting CP defender Gonçalo Inácio. Furthermore, the club have made Real Madrid striker Endrick their No. 1 priority, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, and see the 20-year-old as a better fit for their squad than Club Brugge's Nicolo Tresoldi. Milan are hopeful of using their strong relationship with Los Blancos to explore a loan or permanent signing that would involve a clause which allows the LaLiga side to bring him back to the Bernabéu in the future.

- Manchester United are interested signing in Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils have asked to be kept updated on the 30-year-old's situation, as his representatives are in discussions with multiple clubs regarding a switch in January. The England international is keen to return to Europe and could move on a loan that would include an option to be made permanent. He has also been linked with Crystal Palace.

- Barcelona are facing competition from Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City for the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad, according to Diario Sport. The Blaugrana have been at the front of the queue for the 18-year-old, but there are concerns they may not be able to secure a move for him in January due to the Eredivisie club demanding a fee worth in excess of €20 million, and Premier League sides are now emerging as suitors.

- Arsenal are interested in RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, Football Insider reports. The 21-year-old has been identified as a long-term option by the Gunners, but would require the Bundesliga club to lower their €66 million valuation for a deal to become possible in the January transfer window. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is continuing to assess options to reinforce his side's left flank, while Nusa would be keen on a switch to the Emirates.

- Juventus remain admirers of Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee, with manager Luciano Spalletti hopeful of adding a "physical striker" to his team in January, according to Calciomercato. Zirkzee, 25, is seen as an ideal fit for the Bianconeri's style of play, and he is one of the preferred options of club chief football officer Frederic Massara. United want to move Zirkzee on, and he is open to an exit, while United States international and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun is also on Juve's radar.

articles.headline: Draymond Green swats back at online critics, fuels Warriors' win over Celtics
articles.description: After reinforcing his career​ accolades earlier in the day on social media, Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green closed out an 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday with a last-second defensive stop and rousing celebration from the veteran.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- After engaging in an online back-and-forth about his career​ accolades earlier in the day, Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green closed out an 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday night with a defensive stop on Jayson Tatum at the buzzer, a rousing celebration and a lively postgame news conference.

The Warriors entered having lost five in a row, spiraling down the standings after Stephen Curry tore his oblique to open a recent trip.

Green, in particular, was facing heat because of his lack of offensive punch in Curry's absence, averaging 3.2 points and a career-low 3.2 shot attempts per game in his 15th NBA season.

"I've got to take open shots," Green acknowledged. "But I'm never going to, in Year 15, go, 'Oh, Steph's out, this is my chance.' When I was in Year 6, it was my chance. ... But I would never deduce myself down to, 'Oh, I've got to go score!' That'll never be my mindset."

Green took particular ire to online commentary from former 17-year NBA forward and current Phoenix Suns broadcaster Eddie Johnson, who commented on a social media post about Green's late-career offensive limitations when Curry isn't on the court and questioned that against several players who never made the Hall of Fame.

"You got guys comparing their young selves to my old self," Green said. "It says a lot. You got people flexing their résumés, and if I flex my résumé back, I'm the bully."

Johnson and Green went back and forth over a five-hour span Sunday morning about their careers, including screenshots and potshots. Johnson said he was just doing his job as an analyst and told Green: "Isn't that your main job now and basketball is only when Curry plays?"

Several people within the Warriors predicted an aggressive Green against the Celtics because of three days of rest, the five-game losing streak and Johnson throwing gasoline on the fire.

Green, shifting to the power forward spot, came out firing. In his first 13 games this season -- primarily starting at center -- he didn't make more than a one 3-pointer in any game and never attempted more than two. Against the Celtics, Green attempted four in the first six minutes and hit three of them.

"I don't know if Draymond would want me to share this, but I'll do it anyway because Draymond shares everything with you guys," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. "But he told me on the trip, we talked and he said 'I'll do whatever you need, if you want me to come off the bench, [I will].'"

Kerr told him it wasn't a strategic consideration. Without Curry, Kerr said he felt the Warriors needed to "dig out" of their losing streak on defense and believes Green remains one of the best defensive players in the world.

So, he told Green he was putting center Charles Bassey next to him as a rim protector in the starting lineup and would use him to guard the opponent's best perimeter scorer.

articles.headline: 49ers' Brock Purdy beats Vikings blitz, hears 'MVP' chants in Mexico City
articles.description: Quarterback Brock Purdy heard "MVP" chants in Mexico City and continued to earn praise from his teammates as he led the 49ers to a statement victory against the top-ranked Vikings defense on Sunday night
articles.body:
MEXICO CITY -- As the third quarter ended Sunday night, the majority of the 85,612 people at Estadio Banorte broke out into a chant easy to recognize in any language.

"M-V-P, M-V-P, M-V-P."

The target of their affection? San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, who was in the midst of orchestrating the destruction of the league's No. 1 defense.

By the time Purdy's night was over, he'd led the Niners to a dominant 35-10 victory against the Minnesota Vikings and sent a resounding statement about his Most Valuable Player candidacy on national television.

"Best player in the game right now," receiver Mike Evans said. "He's super dialed in. The way he prepares, the way he competes, he's tough. I always thought he's been underrated."

As the Niners trained in Colorado Springs, Colorado, last week to begin acclimating to the altitude of Mexico City, one of the primary discussion points was how Purdy and Niners coach Kyle Shanahan-led offenses had struggled against Vikings coordinator Brian Flores' defense.

In two previous meetings -- both losses -- the Niners had moved the ball but averaged just 17 points per game. Still, Shanahan projected confidence that Purdy's previous experience against Flores' blitz-happy scheme would prove beneficial the third time around. He was right.

With Flores blitzing Purdy on 20 of his 26 drop backs (77% is the highest rate he has faced in his career), the QB calmly stood in the pocket and delivered big completion after big completion. He finished 17-of-19 for 208 yards and two touchdowns when the Vikings sent more than four pass rushers after him.

After the game, Purdy said the advice he got from Shanahan last week was to trust what he sees and let it rip when the opportunities arise.

"He was just like, 'Dude, you got to be aggressive, don't second guess yourself,'" Purdy said. "Obviously try to read it out as best you can, but you have players out there that can go and get the ball for you, put the ball on them, allow them to go and make plays. And I just feel like our guys did that around me today."

Indeed, Purdy finally played with something at least closer to a full complement of offensive options with Evans returning from Achilles tendinitis and immediately contributing six catches for 109 yards and a touchdown.

But every time Minnesota attempted to take away one of Purdy's options, he found another. He completed passes to nine receivers and finished 21-of-26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions.

Purdy's 98.6 QBR is the third highest in a game by any quarterback this season, trailing only the 99.6 he posted against Miami in Week 2 and the 99.4 Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis had against the Jets in Week 7.

articles.headline: NFL Week 11: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 11.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season began with several blowouts.

With Josh Johnson at quarterback, the Cardinals couldn't get anything going offensively in a loss to the Chiefs. Miami also struggled on that side of the ball against Buffalo in quarterback Kyle McCord's second start. And the Titans' defense allowed touchdowns on the Cowboys' first six drives, leading to a 21-point defeat.

Elsewhere in the early window, the Panthers came out on top of a shootout against the Ravens. The Eagles pulled off an upset over the Steelers with backup quarterback Joe Milton. The Bears won their fifth straight game, while the Lions won in their first game without edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee injury) this season.

In the late window, both New York teams pulled off wins. And Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza almost came back against the Broncos, but a pick-six ended a potential go-ahead drive late in the fourth quarter. The 49ers capped things off Sunday night with a resounding win over the Vikings in Mexico City.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

MIN-SF | JAX-NYG | LV-DEN

NYJ-LAC | BAL-CAR

NO-CHI | PIT-PHI | TB-DET

TEN-DAL | MIA-BUF | ARI-KC

Catch up on Thursday's game:

IND-HOU

San Francisco 35, Minnesota 10

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap | Instant analysis

49ers

Is the 49ers' pass rush ready to take off? The 49ers' defensive line has caught plenty of recent flak for a lack of pressure and production. During their week of practice in Colorado Springs, edge rusher Nick Bosa vowed that he would be better and so, too, would the defensive front. Bosa was right, as the Niners harassed Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins for much of the night. Bosa collected his first sack of the season, and the 49ers' pressure forced several errant Cousins throws, including safety Ji'Ayir Brown's pick-six. The Niners finished with one sack but affected Cousins consistently for most of the night. The Niners pressured Cousins on 15 of 39 dropbacks and he averaged 4.0 yards per attempt with an interception and a sack when San Francisco didn't blitz.

What to make of the QB performance: Brock Purdy undoubtedly heard all the doubts about how he'd fare against Brian Flores' exotic defense after a couple of rough outings previously. But coach Kyle Shanahan said this week that Purdy's previous experience playing against that scheme should help him and that Purdy wouldn't be surprised by anything Flores could throw at him. That proved true Sunday night, as Purdy finished 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. That included 17-of-19 against the blitz with two touchdowns and 12 first downs on the 20 dropbacks in which Minnesota brought five or more pass rushers. -- Nick Wagone

articles.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: Snaps on offense, defense
articles.description: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. The Jaguars have followed through on that, making the 2025 No. 2 overall pick a starter on defense and mixing him in where designed on offense. 

He has started every game at cornerback and has played at least four snaps on offense in all but one game (Week 4 at Cincinnati). He has made big plays on both sides of the ball and had the best game of his career in Week 6, when he clearly showed what kind of threat he can be. Head coach Liam Coen has been consistent in saying that Hunter's offensive usage is fluid.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches, then absolutely will."

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 11 at New York Giants

Hunter played a season-high 73 total snaps (his previous high was 71 in Week 4 against Cincinnati) and a career-high six special teams snaps against the Giants. He played 61 snaps on defense and six on offense, where he touched the ball twice. He had one catch for 3 yards and one rush on an end around that gained 9 yards. It was a quiet day on defense, too, with just six tackles. Hunter has been returning punts in practice, but the Jaguars used Ameer Abdullah in that role against the Giants instead of Parker Washington.

Week 10 at Tennessee Titans

Hunter came up with his highlight play of the season so far with a diving interception of a Cam Ward pass in the first quarter. Ward scrambled to his right on third-and-8 from the Jacksonville 35-yard line and threw back toward the left side of the field for receiver Elic Ayomanor near the sideline, but Hunter snagged the ball and cradled it to his body with his left hand as he hit the ground.

"It was an unbelievable catch, unbelievable play," head coach Liam Coen said. "... Such a special play by obviously a special player."

The Jaguars turned that into an eventual field goal and 10-3 lead early in the second quarter. Hunter, who is tied with cornerback Jourdan Lewis with a team-high three interceptions, played 56 snaps on defense, five on special teams, and five on offense against the Titans. He touched the ball on three of those offensive snaps: An end around that gained 3 yards and two catches for 16 yards.

Week 9 at Baltimore Ravens

It was a quiet night for Hunter on defense -- five tackles on 44 snaps -- but a bad one on offense. Hunter played six snaps on offense and fumbled the only time he touched the ball. Hunter caught a receiver screen from Trevor Lawrence, and Ravens safety Malaki Starks knocked the ball loose 1 yard behind the line of scrimmage. articles.headline: Fantasy buzz: Week 11's leading fantasy scorers through "Sunday Night Football"
articles.description: A closer look at the top 10 fantasy scorers in Week 11, including Cowboys QB Dak Prescott and Broncos RB Jonah Coleman.
articles.body:
Several Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs were among Week 11's leading fantasy scorers, with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and Travis Kelce all in the top five. And then there was Denver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman, who found the end zone three times against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Javonte Williams and George Pickens joined in on the fun in the Cowboys' 21-point rout of Tennessee, while Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson were the other Chiefs to crack the top 10 in the team's easy win over Arizona.

Here's the complete list of the top 10 fantasy scorers for Week 11.

1. Dak Prescott, QB, Dallas Cowboys -- 35.9

2. Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver Broncos -- 34.9

3. CeeDee Lamb, WR, Dallas Cowboys -- 30.2

4. Ashton Jeanty, RB, Las Vegas Raiders -- 27.9

5. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions -- 27.8

6. Chuba Hubbard, RB, Carolina Panthers -- 26.0

7. Travis Kelce, TE, Kansas City Chiefs -- 25.4

8. Patrick Mahomes, QB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 24.96

9. Emmett Johnson, RB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 24.3

10. Javonte Williams, RB, Dallas Cowboys -- 24.1

Click here for the full list of the leading fantasy scorers in Week 11.

Nov. 20: Jones released; Richardson Sr. takes over as starter

With the Indianapolis Colts releasing Daniel Jones, the team will start Anthony Richardson Sr. for the Week 12 matchup versus the New York Giants. So, let's quickly discuss how this impacts the Colts offense from a fantasy perspective.

Richardson brings big-time, dual-threat upside as a runner, as he has posted 640 yards rushing and 10 touchdowns in 19 career games in the league. We should see Richardson's rushing ability used in the Colts' game plan, with more designed carries mixed into the call sheet. However, with a lack of current wide receiver talent in Indy, plus Richardson's accuracy concerns (50.8% career completion rate), he will be a mid-to-lower tier QB2 in my rankings.

Running back Jonathan Taylor, who has scored fewer than 10 points in three of his last four games, could get a slight bump with Richardson as the starter if we get a more run-heavy approach from the Colts, one that also creates cutback lanes and misdirection off the QB read schemes. However, Richardson can also be deployed as a runner near the goal line, which would take away scoring opportunities from Taylor. And I don't see Taylor getting a bump in receiving volume here. Taylor will remain as an RB2 in my rankings simply due to the anticipated rushing volume.

Tight end Tyler Warren scored only 3.2 fantasy points in the Thursday night loss to the Texans (catching one pass for 22 yards), his fourth straight game with fewer than 10 points. Maybe we will see Warren deployed more on seams, corners and third-level throws due to the arm talent of Richardson, but Warren averages only 5.05 air yards per target this season. Until we see the Colts actually cater to the receiving traits of Warren, a quarterback change isn't going to put him back into the TE1 conversation.

-- Matt Bowen

articles.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
articles.description: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
articles.body:
Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.

In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game. Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.

On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks. It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.

Assist your wardrobe with NBA gear from Fanatics

Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.

Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns has 30 points and 13 rebounds as Knicks beat Pacers 113-106
articles.description: — Karl-Anthony Towns had 30 points and 13 rebounds, Jalen Brunson added 22 points, and the New York Knicks beat the Indiana Pacers 113-106 on Sunday night to extend their winning streak to five games.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Karl-Anthony Towns had 30 points and 13 rebounds, Jalen Brunson added 22 points, and the New York Knicks beat the Indiana Pacers 113-106 on Sunday night to extend their winning streak to five games.


              Towns, who missed Saturday night’s buzzer-beater victory over Portland due to an illness, shot 9 for 14 from the field including 4 for 4 on 3-pointers.


              Landry Shamet scored 17 points while Josh Hart finished with 10 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds for the Knicks. It was Hart's 18th triple-double with the Knicks, tying Michael Ray Richardson for second on the team’s career list. Walt Frazier holds the team record with 23. 


              The Knicks were without OG Anunoby, who missed his second straight game because of tightness in his left calf. Backup guard Deuce McBride was held out due to tightness in the left abductor.


              Pascal Siakam scored 25 points, Andrew Nembhard finished with 16 and Ivica Zubac had 10 points and 14 rebounds for the Pacers, who have lost their last four games.


              Towns in the closing minutes of the third quarter outscored Indiana 10-2, capping it off with a 3-pointer that extended the Knicks lead 86-74 with 54 seconds left in the period.


              Indiana fell behind by 12 points after Mikal Bridges hit a 3-pointer that made it 92-80 and trimmed it to 95-87 following a three-point play from Kelly Oubre Jr. with 7:31 left in the fourth quarter.


              A fadeaway jumper from Brunson increased the Knicks advantage to 110-95 — their largest lead of the night — with 2:35 remaining.


              The Pacers kept it close and went on a 6-0 run capped by a layup from Obi Toppin that made it 112-106 with 25 seconds remaining.


              Brunson then put the game out of reach with a free throw after Quenton Jackson was called for a foul away from the ball.


              Up Next
              Pacers: Host Oklahoma City on Monday night.


              Knicks: Continue their five-game homestand against Cleveland on Wednesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: USMNT's Cardoso scores as Atlético ease to win over Getafe
articles.description: Atlético Madrid bolstered their spot in third in LaLiga with a comfortable 3-0 win at Getafe on Sunday.
articles.body:
Atlético Madrid bolstered their spot in third in LaLiga with a comfortable 3-0 win at Getafe on Sunday.

A superb long-range strike by Álex Baena put Diego Simeone's team in front and Johnny Cardoso's 30th-minute tap-in increased Atlético's stranglehold on the contest in Madrid.

Getafe pushed for a way back into the contest, but Atlético stood firm and grabbed a third late on from the penalty spot via Alejandro Grimaldo to make it eight wins in nine league matches.

It took Atlético only 10 minutes to break the deadlock when Julián Álvarez controlled inside the area and teed up Baena, who let fly from 30 yards and found the bottom corner.

Atlético went close again immediately after from a corner, but Getafe's fortunate ended there with Cardoso able to double the visitors' lead in the 30th minute.

Álvarez sent in a dangerous delivery which Getafe goalkeeper David Soria failed to gather and Cardoso tapped in on the line.

Getafe pushed to reduce the deficit, but it remained 2-0 at halftime.

Simeone replaced Cardoso with Lee Kang-In for the second half and Baena almost made it 3-0 with one shot saved before he sent another off target.

Baena and Álvarez were taken off midway through the second half, but there was still time for Atlético to grab a third.

After substitute Alexander Sørloth headed wide, the Norwegian was brought down inside the area by Djene Dakonam and after a VAR review, Dakonam was sent off and Alejandro Grimaldo converted from 12 yards to move Atlético to 31 points on the season, two behind Real Madrid and five behind leaders Barcelona.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
articles.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool, insisting Leny Yoro's early challenge on Alexander Isak was "never a red card."

Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute by referee Sam Barrott for what was deemed a last-man foul that denied Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

The Reds went on to complete a comprehensive rout over the 10 men with further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz as Mauricio Pochettino's Red Devils reign got off to a miserable start at Anfield.

The new head coach said he took full ownership of the result but felt the Yoro sending off changed the course of the game, with his skipper in agreement and feeling the wrong decision had been reached.

The Portugal midfielder told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

articles.headline: Villarreal deny Nicolas Pépé eye surgery was due to viewing solar eclipse
articles.description: Villarreal have denied that Nicolas Pépé underwent eye surgery as a result of viewing the solar eclipse.
articles.body:
Villarreal have denied that Nicolas Pépé underwent eye surgery as a result of viewing the solar eclipse.

The Ivorian winger missed five games in October after undergoing the surgery, but the LaLiga club have refuted reports that this was due to viewing the phenomenon without the proper protection.

Such reports surfaced after footage on social media -- allegedly posted by Pépé himself -- appeared to show the former Arsenal man looking directly at the eclipse on Aug. 12, 2026, without a solar viewer.

"In light of recent reports published by various media outlets, Villarreal CF wishes to clarify that claims linking Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery to viewing the solar eclipse are completely false," the club said in a statement on Sunday.

"The procedure had been scheduled beforehand for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club calls for accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters concerning the health of its players."

Villarreal lost to both Liverpool and Real Madrid during the period in which Pépé was absent.

The 31-year-old has scored three goals in 12 games this season after one of the best campaigns of his career in 2025-26, in which he notched eight goals and 11 assists in 46 matches.

- Flick: Barcelona comeback against Villarreal 'unbelievable' but not happy with ref

- Carlos Espí's 'most special' goal earns Real Madrid win and Rafael Nadal praise

- Olley: Arsenal's near-collapse at Newcastle is a wake-up call

He joined Villarreal in 2024 from Trabzonspor after previously playing for the likes of Arsenal, Lille and Nice.

Iñigo Pérez's side are 10th in LaLiga having won four, drawn three and lost six matches.
